evidence.excerpt: Cohort 46 Application Information Webinar: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 10:30am - 12:00pm PST.

The Nurse Residency Program is for new graduate registered nurses who have graduated from an accredited nursing program within 19 months of the residency start date and have less than six months of paid registered nurse work experience.
Current California RN License is required prior to the start date of the residency program.
Fall Cohort application typically opens in February or March. Spring Cohort application typically opens in September.
Designed for newly licensed nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) or Master of Science in Nursing (MSN).
The Alan & Marlene Norton Nurse Residency Program enrolls cohorts in January and August. Application cycles occur prior to each cohort start.
The Alan & Marlene Norton Nurse Residency Program is designed for new graduate registered nurses with less than one year of nursing experience.

Thank you for your interest in our Nurse Residency Program, a program focused on the New Graduate Nurse. Our Residency Program is offered three times per year: spring (February), summer (August) and fall (October).
Next program start date is October 19, 2026. Nurse Resident positions will be posted beginning August 18, 2026. Positions may close externally based on applicant volume.
Can I apply for a Nurse Residency position before I get my RN license? Yes. However, you must have your CA RN license by the program start date.

evidence.excerpt: Cohort 46 Information Webinar: Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm PST. Applications for Cohort 46 are anticipated to open in mid-October 2026.
The Stanford Health Care Nurse Residency Program welcomes new graduate registered nurses who have graduated from an accredited BSN or MSN program within the last 18 months.
The UCSF Health New Nurse Residency Training Program (NNRTP) supports new graduate registered nurses through their first year of clinical practice.
The UCI Health Transition to Practice Nurse Residency Program offers evidence-based curriculum and preceptorship for new graduate registered nurses entering acute care.
The Sharp HealthCare Nurse Residency Program accepts new graduate nurses for training across acute care specialties. The Spring 2027 cohort is currently in planning stages.

The Scripps New Graduate RN Training Program is a 40-week system-wide program providing clinical coaching, mentorship, and classroom education for new graduate registered nurses with 6 months or less of experience.
The New Graduate RN Program at Hoag Hospital is a 12-month program based on Benner Novice to Expert model, challenging new graduate nurses to transition into clinical practice.
Keck Medicine of USC offers a structured Nurse Residency Program accredited with distinction by ANCC PTAP for new graduate novice nurses entering acute care clinical practice.
The Kaiser Permanente Nurse Residency Program is a 12-month evidence-based transition to practice program for newly licensed new graduate registered nurses.
The National Nurse Residency Program (NNRP) supports the transition of newly licensed new graduate registered nurses from student to professional RN across Dignity Health and CommonSpirit facilities.

The Adventist Health Nurse Residency Program is a structured one-year orientation and professional development program designed to support new graduate registered nurses in their transition to professional practice.
